question: In public health, what age group is generally referred to as adolescents?
explanation: Spot on! The World Health Organization defines adolescence as the teenage years spanning from 10 to 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why do young women and girls often face a higher risk of new HIV infections in many communities?

options.A: Males do not contract the virus due to protective antibodies.
options.B: Biological differences and social inequalities intersect to increase their risk.
options.C: Healthcare workers screen boys less frequently than girls.
options.D: Females possess a genetic immunity that wears off during puberty.

explanation: Well done! Young women face both physical vulnerabilities and social factors like gender inequality that make it harder to negotiate safe sex. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which part of the teenage brain is still maturing and plays a big role in impulse control and risk-taking?
explanation: Correct! The prefrontal cortex develops slowly into early adulthood, which explains why teenagers sometimes struggle with weighing long-term consequences. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why is a 16-year-old girl biologically more vulnerable to catching an STI during intercourse?

options.A: Rapid regeneration of damaged epithelial tissue
options.B: Excessive production of thick, protective mucus lining
options.C: Complete absence of white blood cells in the vaginal canal
options.D: Cervical ectopy with a larger area of vulnerable cells

explanation: You got it! Teenage reproductive tracts have cervical ectopy, exposing delicate cells that make it easier for germs to enter. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h2)

question: What are the common signs of a Chlamydia infection in a young female?

options.A: Painless hard sores on the palms
options.B: High fever and generalized skin rash

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia often causes irritation in the cervix and urethra, leading to unusual discharge and painful urination (dysuria). [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why do nurses recommend routine STI screenings for sexually active teens even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pathogens disappear on their own within one week.
options.B: Many common infections do not show any noticeable symptoms.
options.C: Symptoms only appear after permanent organ damage occurs.
options.D: Testing builds immunity against future pathogen exposures.

explanation: Exactly! Infections like chlamydia are often 'silent' or asymptomatic in young people, so testing is the only way to catch them early. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which key immune cells are primarily attacked and destroyed by HIV?
explanation: Correct! HIV specifically targets CD4+ T-cells, using them to make copies of itself and gradually weakening the body's immune defense. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h4)

question: What typically happens during the clinical latency stage of an untreated HIV infection?

options.A: The immune system completely clears the virus from the body.
options.B: The patient immediately develops terminal opportunistic infections.
options.C: The virus replicates slowly while the patient may have few symptoms.
options.D: Red blood cells multiply rapidly to compensate for tissue damage.

explanation: Well done! During latency, the virus is still active but multiplies at a low level, and the person might feel completely well for years without treatment. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using the '5 Ps' framework when taking an adolescent's health history?

options.A: To calculate the exact body mass index of the patient
options.B: To determine the nutritional requirements of the teenager
options.C: To gather a thorough and structured sexual health history
options.D: To diagnose mental health disorders like depression

explanation: Spot on! The 5 Ps (Partners, Practices, Protection, Past history, Pregnancy prevention) help nurses collect sexual health details in an organized, non-judgmental way. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h5)

question: A nurse wants to test a 15-year-old patient for Chlamydia. Which diagnostic test is the most sensitive and reliable?
explanation: Correct! NAATs are the gold standard for spotting bacterial STIs like chlamydia using a simple urine sample or swab. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for adolescents living with HIV?

options.A: To suppress viral replication and preserve immune function
options.B: To stimulate appetite and cause weight gain
options.C: To replace damaged bone marrow cells permanently
options.D: To cure the infection completely within a few weeks

explanation: You got it! ART keeps the virus levels super low, allowing the immune system to stay strong and protect the body. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why must nurses emphasize treating sexual partners when a teenager is diagnosed with a bacterial STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection of the original patient and control community spread
options.B: To ensure the laboratory technicians have enough test samples
options.C: To fulfill mandatory legal requirements for school attendance
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing antibiotics

explanation: Spot on! Treating partners stops the 'ping-pong' effect where partners pass the infection right back to each other. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h6)

question: Which feature is essential when setting up adolescent-friendly health services?

options.B: High service fees to cover facility costs
options.D: Mandatory parental presence for all visits

explanation: Correct! Teens are much more likely to visit clinics and open up when they know their private medical info is kept strictly confidential. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h7)

question: How do peer support groups help teenagers living with a chronic condition like HIV?

options.A: They eliminate the side effects of antiretroviral medications.
options.B: They replace the need for professional nursing assessments entirely.
options.C: They reduce feelings of isolation and encourage treatment adherence.
options.D: They provide financial loans for higher education expenses.

explanation: Well done! Connecting with others facing the same journey helps teens share tips, stay on their meds, and realize they aren't alone. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is one of the biggest barriers stopping adolescents from seeking STI testing and treatment?

options.A: Too many hours spent in school classes
options.C: Overabundance of trained nurses in clinics
options.D: Fear of social stigma and judgment

explanation: Correct! Fear of being judged or gossiped about often makes teenagers keep quiet and delay getting the medical help they need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h8)

question: A community health nurse wants to protect HIV-negative teens who are at high risk of exposure. Which preventive medication should the nurse discuss?
explanation: Spot on! PrEP involves taking daily anti-HIV medications to significantly lower the chances of catching the virus. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h8)
